text: Write a very short story that begins with someone finding a key that doesn't fit any lock in their house.
Write a very short story about the last phone call ever made.
Write a very short story in which a lighthouse keeper receives a letter addressed to the lighthouse itself.
Write a very short story about two neighbors who have never spoken and the wall they share.
Write a very short story where the weather forecast is always right about one family and no one else.
Write a very short story about an object in a museum that remembers being used.
Write a very short story that takes place entirely during a red traffic light.
Write a very short story about a translator who begins to suspect one language contains a word the other refuses to hold.
Write a very short story in which someone inherits a debt of a highly unusual kind.
Write a very short story about the first morning after a city's bells all stop.
Write a very short story where a child teaches an old machine a game.
Write a very short story about a map that is accurate except for one deliberate mistake.
List five genuinely different uses for a brick that a hardware store would never advertise. One sentence each.
List five genuinely different uses for a broken umbrella. One sentence each.
List five genuinely different uses for yesterday's newspaper in a house with no fireplace. One sentence each.
List five genuinely different uses for a single chopstick. One sentence each.
List five genuinely different uses for a dead smartphone that will never turn on again. One sentence each.
List five genuinely different uses for a piano that can no longer be tuned. One sentence each.
Explain what memory is to someone who has never forgotten anything, using one extended comparison.
Describe the internet to a lighthouse keeper from 1890, using one extended comparison drawn from their world.
Invent a new holiday and describe how it is celebrated, in one paragraph.
Describe the feeling of waiting for important news, without naming any emotion directly.
Explain why songs get stuck in heads, as if the explanation were a nature documentary about an animal.
Write a one-paragraph recipe for an impossible dish (for example: preserved morning fog). Ingredients and steps.
